claim: The thermal array cannot resolve a face or a number plate from 4.3 m: under the IEC 62676-4 detection level at head height
law: Pixels per metre = 1 / (range x pixel angle); IEC 62676-4 levels detect 25, recognise 125, identify 250 px/m

claim: One pole covers a 3 m sidewalk, a 2 m bike lane and the nearest 3.5 m lane (110 degree axis across the street)
law: Ray geometry of the 110 x 75 degree lens, tilt 7.5 degrees toward the road
check: 10.9 deg margin on the sidewalk side >= 0 deg margin on the sidewalk side
closed_by: CBC-CAL-001 A2, A3 (10.9 deg margin on the sidewalk side)

claim: A person stands out from pavement by more than the single-frame detection contrast on a mild design day
law: Surface energy balance and the array's noise: NETD 0.1 K RMS at 1 Hz (Melexis MLX90640 datasheet) scales as the square root of the refresh rate; 4 sigma on a person that fills 0.37 of a pixel behind a 0.75 transmission window
check: smallest contrast 5.3 K; blind 10.2 h a day on sunlit pavement with single frames, 3.2 h with track averaging, 0.0 h shaded (assumed surface temperatures, to measure)

claim: A 0.5 mm unpigmented HDPE film passes at least 0.5 of 8 to 14 um radiation
law: Two Fresnel reflections (n 1.53) and bulk absorption of 4 per cm, band-averaged (assumed; polyethylene is known to be IR transparent, thin film transmits most of the band)
check: 0.75 transmission >= 0.5 transmission

claim: A car at 50 km/h stays in the field for the 4 frames the tracker needs
law: Frames = field length / speed x frame rate (8 full frames a second from 16 Hz subpages). CAL-001 C1 treats the car as a point at road level (4.2 frames); the warm hood is about 1.0 m up, where the along-street field shrinks by (4.3 - 1.0) / 4.3 (independent review)
check: 4.2 frames at road level, 3.2 at the hood, against 4: fails. Fix proposed: 32 Hz subpages (16 frames a second) give 6.4, at 1 MHz I2C (bus 24 % busy at 16 Hz, 48 % at 32 Hz, CAL-001 F1), noise up by the square root of 2 (recovered by track averaging) and a faster pull-up (644 ohm, F2); this changes the sensor port speed of the shared FieldNode core, so it goes to Amish (CBC-DEC-001 O3)

claim: Winter solar harvest covers the daily load (6 W panel, 1.5 peak sun hours, 40 % derating)
law: Stored energy = panel W x sun hours x derating x MPPT efficiency x charge efficiency
check: 4.36 Wh/day >= 2.47 Wh/day
closed_by: CBC-CAL-001 E3 (4.4 Wh against 2.47 Wh, while the cell can charge: see S8, S25)

claim: One cell carries the node for 3 days without sun
law: Usable energy = 3.2 V x 6 Ah x 80 % depth of discharge; load 103 mW average; 70 % capacity at -20 C and 80 % at end of life (independent review: both together)
check: 3 days (-20 C, end of life) <= 3.49 days (-20 C, end of life)
closed_by: CBC-CAL-001 E2 (4.36 days at -20 C; 3.49 days with the end-of-life 80 % as well)

claim: The node stays energy neutral through a winter at sites where the air falls below freezing
law: LiFePO4 cells must not be charged below 0 C (lithium plating); FieldNode's NTC lockout stops charging. First-order enclosure temperature in winter sun: (0.4 x 300 W/m2 x 0.05 m2 x 0.6 shade + 0.1 W) / 1.2 W/K = 3.1 K above the air (assumptions)
check: by this estimate the cell can charge only when the air is above about -3 C, and nearer 0 C allowing for the thermal lag of the cell after a cold night (independent review), so 0 C is taken as the limit; below that the node lives on the stored 4.4 days and then stops, so energy neutrality holds for cool sites, not for a Toronto January. The claim fails for cold sites; fixes (heated cell pocket, low-temperature cell) change the shared FieldNode core and the scope, so they go to Amish (CBC-DEC-001 O1)

claim: The 10-byte record fits US915 DR0 and its airtime stays under the 400 ms dwell limit
law: LoRa time on air (Semtech AN1200.13) for 10 + 13 bytes at SF10, 125 kHz; US915 DR0 allows 11 bytes

claim: Uplinks stay inside the EU868 1 % duty cycle
law: Airtime per hour = 4 x time on air at SF9 (206 ms)

claim: Six 12-bit counters hold a 15-minute count in the busiest lane
law: Nearest lane at 1,800 vehicles/h (saturation flow, assumed) is 450 per 15 min; a 12-bit counter holds 4,095
check: 450 counts per bin <= 4095 counts per bin

claim: Wind load: the post carries the panel at 35 m/s gusts with a safety factor of 1.5
law: Drag = 0.5 rho v2 Cf A; bending of a 42.4 x 3 mm aluminium post, 6063-T6 yield 150 MPa
check: 2.7 MPa <= 100 MPa

claim: The band saddles hold the arm against the twist of the wind on arm and head
law: Friction torque of two bands at 1,000 N preload each, mu 0.2 (assumed) against the wind torque; if the liners creep and half the preload is lost the factor falls to about 1.6 (independent review), so a re-torque interval is needed

claim: The counter weighs 6 kg or less on the pole
law: Sum of modelled volumes times density plus catalogue masses of bought parts

claim: The I2C bus runs at 400 kHz over the 2 m M12 cable
law: Rise time 0.8473 R C <= 300 ns (I2C fast mode) with 220 pF of cable (100 pF/m assumed, to measure): pull-up of at most 1.6 kohm, sink current 2 mA (within the 3 mA limit)
check: 1.5 kohm pull-up <= 1.61 kohm pull-up

claim: The STM32WL runs the fixed-point tracker (about 150 cycles per pixel, 2 % of a 48 MHz core, about 40 kB of RAM)
law: Operation counts: 768 pixels x 150 cycles x 8 frames/s / 48 MHz; RAM tally of CBC-CAL-001 F4 (64 kB part); the vendor's floating-point conversion would not fit (50 % of the core)
check: cycle count is an estimate until the tracker is profiled on the part (TRL 4, on hold)

claim: Parts cost stays within the USD 275 value-engineering target
law: Sum of the 14 BOM lines (indicative prices; thermal array USD 64.95 at SparkFun, checked 2026-10-31)
check: 274 USD <= 275 USD

claim: The window film survives five years of sun
law: Unstabilised polyethylene photo-oxidises and embrittles under UV; carbon black would stop it but also blocks the infrared, so a UV-stabilised (hindered amine) clear grade is needed
check: no grade chosen; film to be specified and measured (TRL 4, on hold)

claim: Aluminium saddles, plates and arm with stainless bands and bolts last five years on a steel street pole
law: Aluminium is anodic to stainless steel and to a steel pole in a wet, salted street; the contacts are small and painted or coated in practice, but the joints are not specified
check: isolating washers or coating to specify; to confirm in the build plan checks (TRL 4, on hold)

claim: The counter records no image and no personal identifier: only six counters leave the device in normal operation
law: No personal data can be recovered from 7.6 px/m thermal frames held in RAM and overwritten every 125 ms; the record identifies no one (data protection by design, GDPR Article 25). During an aim check the calibration jumper streams frames to a laptop at the pole (CBC-CAL-001 H6, PR-020), and quiet night-time bins can single out one person (independent review)
check: S1 gives the resolution; the firmware path for the jumper stream, its limits and the small-count bins are firmware design and audit questions (TRL 4, on hold)

claim: Option A at temperate sites: the cell stays below its 45 C charge limit
law: Enclosure temperature = air + 3.1 K (S8 estimate) with the temperate design day capped at 20 C air (PR-008); LiFePO4 charging allowed 0 to 45 C (cell datasheet class)
check: 23 C <= 45 C; on a hot clear day outside this scope FieldNode's own figures give 0.8 Wh stored against 2.47 Wh drawn without a shield (CBC-CAL-001 E6)

claim: The window stays clear of dew, frost, insects and droppings
law: A film of water or frost on the window absorbs 8 to 14 um radiation strongly (a 10 um water film is estimated to pass about 0.37 by the independent review; not recomputed here); webs, insects and droppings block pixels
check: no heater, hydrophobic coating or wiper is in the design; contrast margin (S3) and cleaning interval to measure (TRL 4, on hold)

claim: The 2 m sensor cable and the node survive surges and electrostatic discharge on a street pole
law: A cable running up a pole is exposed to induced surges and static discharge; the BOM has resettable fuses (line 14) but no surge protection devices
check: protection to specify with the FieldNode project; to assess (TRL 4, on hold)

claim: The tracker classes people, bicycles and cars correctly and does not count dogs, umbrellas or prams as extra people
law: Class by blob area, speed and track length at 32 x 24 pixels; a dog or a pram is a small warm blob, an umbrella can hide a person from above (independent review)
check: no calculation possible at TRL 3; replay of recorded frames at TRL 4 (on hold); tracked in CBC-RSK-001 F9

claim: Option B: RF exposure of a person under the radar is far below the ICNIRP limit
law: Power density = EIRP / (4 pi r2) at head height, 2.40 m, with 1 W EIRP (a deliberate overestimate); ICNIRP 2020 general public limit 10 W/m2 above 6 GHz (to confirm against the guideline text)

claim: Option B: a 20 W panel keeps the radar head energy neutral in winter (radar frames duty-cycled to 0.2 W average; running continuously at 1.2 W it drew 32 Wh/day and failed)
law: Stored energy of a 20 W panel (1.5 peak sun hours, 40 % derating) against the daily draw; fix decided under the standing instruction (CBC-DEC-001 C1): one frame burst in six. TI's reference may draw more than 1.2 W and the burst rate the tracker needs is unproven (independent review)
check: 5.3 Wh/day <= 14.5 Wh/day stored on paper; the burst rate that still gives 4 frames per vehicle is to be profiled (TRL 4, on hold)

claim: Option B: two cells carry the radar head for 3 days without sun (0.2 W duty-cycled average; at 0.25 W they gave only 2.6 days with cold and end of life together and failed)
law: Usable energy of two 3.2 V 6 Ah cells at 80 % against the duty-cycled draw, 70 % capacity at -20 C and 80 % at end of life, together (independent review)
check: 3 days (-20 C, end of life) <= 3.22 days (-20 C, end of life)

claim: Option B: a 60 GHz radar counts people and vehicles by range, angle and speed in rain, dark and heat
law: FMCW radar resolves range from the beat frequency and speed from phase; Texas Instruments offers a people counting and tracking reference for the IWR6843 (TI, checked 2026-10-31)
check: the principle is established; counting accuracy and false counts from wind-blown foliage are not shown (TRL 4, on hold)

claim: Option B stays at 6 kg or less on the pole
law: Option A's 5.24 kg plus the CAD mass difference between the two models (0.4 kg: second cell, larger panel, radar head); the independent review put it nearer 6.8 kg, to profile

claim: Option B: FieldNode's charger passes the 20 W panel's current into two cells
law: Peak charge current of a 20 W panel at 1,000 W/m2 is 5.0 A (CBC-CAL-001 E5) against FieldNode's standard charger setting of 1.5 A; two cells in parallel take 2.5 A each (0.42 C)
check: the charger setting caps the harvest unless FieldNode's high-load variant (raised in CBC-DDR-001 D3) is used; a shared-core change, so it goes to Amish with option B (CBC-DEC-001 O4)

claim: Option B at hot sites: the cell can still charge when the air is near 40 C
law: LiFePO4 charging is allowed to 45 C only (cell datasheet class); FieldNode's own figures put the cell above the limit for most sun hours on a hot clear day and store 0.8 Wh against 2.47 Wh drawn without a shield, 13.1 Wh with its proposed shield (CBC-CAL-001 E6)
check: option B is the hot-climate variant but shares the same cell and enclosure, so it needs the shield or a cell pack in shade; a shared-core change, so it goes to Amish with option B (CBC-DEC-001 O4)
